metadata.title: On Sets of Integers Containing No k Elements in Arithmetic Progression (Szemeredi, 1975)
metadata.framework: Combinatorial proof that subsets of integers with positive upper density contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions, using the Szemeredi regularity lemma
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of Szemeredi (1975). Pre-arXiv publication.

nodes.name: Upper density of a subset of integers
nodes.statement: The upper density of $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ is $\bar{d}(A) = \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}|}{N}$. A set has positive upper density if $\bar{d}(A) > 0$.

nodes.name: Arithmetic progression of length k
nodes.statement: A $k$-term arithmetic progression (AP) is a sequence $a, a+d, a+2d, \ldots, a+(k-1)d$ with $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $d > 0$.

nodes.name: Szemeredi's theorem
nodes.statement: For every integer $k \geq 1$ and every $\delta > 0$, there exists $N_0(k, \delta)$ such that every subset $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ with $|A| \geq \delta N$ and $N \geq N_0$ contains a $k$-term arithmetic progression.

nodes.name: Szemeredi regularity lemma
nodes.statement: For every $\epsilon > 0$, every sufficiently large graph $G$ can be partitioned into $k$ parts (where $k \leq T(\epsilon)$ for some tower function $T$) such that all but $\epsilon$-fraction of pairs of parts form $\epsilon$-regular bipartite graphs (the edge density between any large subsets of the two parts is close to the overall density between them).

nodes.name: Szemeredi's proof strategy
nodes.statement: The proof is highly combinatorial and uses: (1) the regularity lemma to partition $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ into structured pieces, (2) a counting lemma showing that regular partitions contain the expected number of APs, and (3) a density increment argument. The proof is notoriously complex and led to several alternative proofs (Furstenberg 1977, Gowers 2001).

nodes.name: History and significance
nodes.statement: Szemeredi's theorem was conjectured by Erdos and Turan (1936). Special cases: $k=3$ proved by Roth (1953) using Fourier analysis. The full theorem has inspired vast developments in combinatorics, ergodic theory (Furstenberg), and additive combinatorics (Gowers norms).

nodes.name: Quantitative bounds
nodes.statement: The bound $N_0(k, \delta)$ from Szemeredi's proof is tower-type (iterated exponential). Gowers (1997) showed this tower-type dependence is unavoidable for the regularity lemma itself, though the AP theorem may admit better bounds.
